gloss: to reach the age of awareness; to become old enough to understand things

definitions.gloss: to reach the age of awareness; to become old enough to understand the world around one
definitions.explanation: Describes the developmental stage when a young child becomes capable of understanding and remembering their surroundings, typically around ages 3-5. Almost always used with reference to one's earliest memories.

examples.japanese: {物心|ものごころ}ついたときには{父|ちち}はいなかった。
examples.english: By the time I was old enough to be aware, my father was already gone.

examples.japanese: {物心|ものごころ}つく{前|まえ}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}したので、{生|う}まれた{町|まち}の{記憶|きおく}がない。
examples.english: We moved before I was old enough to remember, so I have no memories of the town where I was born.

examples.japanese: {物心|ものごころ}ついたころから{音楽|おんがく}が{好|す}きだった。
examples.english: I've loved music for as long as I can remember.

notes:
Composed of {物心|ものごころ} (awareness of the world, understanding of things) + つく (to become attached, to develop). A common expression in autobiographical narratives and family stories. {物心|ものごころ} itself is a compound of {物|もの} (things) + {心|こころ} (heart/mind).

Almost always appears in fixed temporal patterns like {物心|ものごころ}ついたとき (when I became aware), {物心|ものごころ}つく{前|まえ} (before I was aware), or {物心|ものごころ}ついたころ (around the time I became aware).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {物心|ものごころ}ついたときには: by the time one was old enough to understand
- {物心|ものごころ}つく{前|まえ}に: before one was old enough to remember
- {物心|ものごころ}ついたころから: from as far back as one can remember
- {物心|ものごころ}がつく: to develop awareness (with が particle)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {記憶|きおく}がある{限|かぎ}り: as far as one can remember — focuses on memory rather than developmental stage
- {幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}: when one was young — a general time reference without the developmental milestone nuance
